title: Flour Tortillas (Soft & Chewy)
description: Soft, chewy, and beautifully pliable, these traditional flour tortillas are made using a simple dough of flour, fat, and warm water. Resting the dough and cooking on a hot skillet creates tender tortillas perfect for tacos, burritos, wraps, and quesadillas.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: All-purpose flour (high quality, 11–12% protein preferred) – 500 g (4 cups)
Baking powder – 7 g (2 tsp, optional, for a slightly puffier tortilla)
Lard – 75 g (⅓ cup, traditional) or neutral vegetable shortening (substitute: butter or neutral oil, but lard gives the best flavor & chew)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Mix the Dough
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together flour, salt, and baking powder.
Add the lard and rub it into the flour with fingertips until the texture resembles coarse sand.
Slowly add warm water while mixing until a shaggy dough forms.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Knead for Gluten Development
steps: Transfer to a clean surface and knead 8–10 minutes until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky but not sticky.
Dough should pass a soft windowpane test (stretches without tearing).
Cover with a damp towel and rest 30 minutes (allows gluten to relax for better rolling).

instruction.title: Step 3 – Divide and Rest
steps: Divide dough into 12 equal portions (about 65–70 g each).
Cover and rest 20 minutes at room temp.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Rolling
steps: On a lightly floured surface, roll each ball into a thin circle, 8–9 inches wide.
Rotate often to keep shape even.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Cooking
steps: Heat a heavy cast iron skillet or flat comal over medium-high heat until very hot.
Place one tortilla on the skillet; cook 30–45 seconds until bubbles form and golden brown spots appear.
Stack cooked tortillas in a clean towel to keep warm and steamy (this keeps them soft).

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve warm with tacos, burritos, fajitas, quesadillas, or wraps.
Excellent alongside grilled meats, beans, rice, or Mexican stews.
Brush lightly with butter for extra richness if serving on their own.

chefTips: Fat choice matters: Lard = authentic flavor + chew; shortening = neutral; butter = richer but slightly less chewy.
Hydration is key: Slightly wetter dough makes softer tortillas. Adjust water if flour is very dry.
Resting twice: First rest builds extensibility; second rest ensures thin rolling without shrinkage.
Keep warm: Stacking in a towel keeps tortillas pliable for hours.
Reheat properly: Briefly on a hot skillet, never microwave uncovered (they’ll dry out).
